title: RAW UNREVIEWED: chey tal retrieves an earlier stage-scoped process plan for a new written input
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_UNTESTED. Rival to physical-material replacement: a written chey tal call may retrieve a ProcessPlan from the immediately preceding complete paragraph and execute a fixed selected stage with a new explicit input. CoReMA gr1.218 as-before context supplies a historical reason to distinguish method reuse from copying prior ingredients; its unresolved stage/reference scope remains. Only written call-to-execution-to-new-result dependency can distinguish this hypothesis.

design.mechanism: TAL is hypothesized as a typed earlier-ProcessPlan reference; CHEY as its invocation construction. A complete preceding native paragraph must actually declare an ordered Plan with formal input slots and steps. One globally frozen stage selector retrieves the permitted subplan; explicit current-paragraph input binds the same formal slots. Invocation generates new event IDs and a result record for the current input, consumed by an actual later written continuation. No previous ingredients, previously produced material or ambient result is copied unless separately written and priced.
design.unit: Prospectively select current complete native paragraph containing exact chey tal plus exactly the immediately preceding complete paragraph, by existing metadata before opening bodies. No target unit or preceding boundary is newly queried/nominated here. Root fixes discovery/application partitions and retains every reader, uncertain native flag and missing-pair alternate.
design.contrast: Typed METHOD_REF -> APPLY(PlanStage,current_input) -> new event/result versus FV MATERIAL_REF -> replacement MaterialSpec -> dependent material consumers; RAW851 instead refers to an earlier result as the next input. Component-plus-attached-protocol and full-plan versus stage-plan variants are separately costed rivals, not silently excluded.
design.prediction: Changing only the explicitly current input preserves the retrieved stage/operation order and creates an execution/result with the new input provenance. Earlier ingredient slots are not donated to the caller. A later written consumer must use that produced result/event rather than a prior result or preloaded material. A bare material-reference output cannot meet a frozen Plan invocation signature without an explicitly paid material-to-protocol bridge.
design.scope: Raw C0 interpretation of the exact two-group construction only. No universal CHEY/TAL gloss, substring writer, sentence boundary, source-copy code, statistical likelihood, semantic confirmation or application body access.
